item.title: The Team You Didn't Hire
item.description: Five bots doing the jobs a startup used to hire a whole team for.

item.title: Herd your whole fleet of Grok bots from one chat
item.description: Once you run more than one Grok bot, keeping tabs on all of them is its own job. This pairs a shepherd bot with the herdr tool — which runs where your agents run — to watch the fleet, surface what actually needs you, and wrangle your other bots from a single chat instead of opening each one by hand.

item.title: Screen your X replies for burners and insults
item.description: Reviews the replies to your posts and splits the signal from the noise: it flags accounts under 100 followers or under a year old, plus anyone slinging insults, so real conversation stays visible and throwaway replies get moderated. Jason Calacanis built it to keep his mentions classy.

item.title: X Account Management
item.description: Six shared Bots to run — and quietly read — your whole X account.

item.title: iMessage for Grok Bot
item.description: Read, triage, search, and send iMessages from a local macOS helper.

item.title: PostOnce
item.description: Connect a Grok bot to the socials you already run and draft posts from chat.

item.title: ContentDrips
item.description: Let your agent design on-brand LinkedIn and Instagram carousels from chat.

item.title: Create a branded carousel from a single topic
item.description: Give Grok Bot a topic such as how to price freelance work. With ContentDrips MCP connected, it builds a multi-slide carousel in your saved brand style (or a named template), returns the editor link, and waits for you before any LinkedIn or Instagram publish.

item.title: Everything you need to know about Grok Bot templates
item.description: A Grok Bot template is a shareable blueprint for a Bot. Open one link and Grok Bot creates a new copy with the original role, skills, routines, and supported integrations. Your chats, logins, and secrets stay private.

item.title: BulkPublish
item.description: Let your agent schedule and publish social posts across 15 networks.

item.title: Run a faceless YouTube channel: source, edit, caption and schedule
item.description: A faceless channel is a production line - find raw material, cut a short, add captions, make a thumbnail, upload. RoundtableSpace flagged Grok Bot running the whole line. This is the version with a human gate: the bot does the repetitive work, you approve before anything publishes, on content you have rights to use.

item.title: A shareable bot that screens every pitch deck against your own criteria
item.description: Brian Evans gets pitched 5-10 times a week, so he built a Grok Bot that learns exactly what he looks for and scores each deck against it - filtering the misfits before he spends a minute. He built it on Grok Bot's new shareable-templates feature, which strips your data so the workflow can be handed to someone else.

item.title: Turn ten years of calendar meetings into a Notion CRM, automatically
item.description: Gaurav Munjal pointed Grok Bot at ten years of his calendar and told it to build a Notion database of every person he ever met - each with their LinkedIn, what they're doing now, and tags. It ran 2.5 hours straight and logged ~1,000 people from the first three years alone. A back-office job no human ever gets to.

item.title: Sightkick
item.description: Run SEO end to end: AI-answer visibility, articles, publishing, Search Console proof.

item.title: See what the market is pricing in before the crowd reacts to it
item.description: Now that Grok Bot reads live prices and option chains, most will ask 'should I buy NVDA'. Alex Prompter uses it as an expectations desk: it reads the ATM straddle to show the market's expected move before earnings and Fed days, contrasts it with the headlines, and names which side has to be wrong. Read-only by design.

item.title: Eight named bots run the whole fund: research, trading, risk and back office
item.description: RohOnChain's field-report paper argues a fund's headcount moat has collapsed: research desk, trading, and back office map onto eight named bots on one shared cloud computer. The twist is build order - business-operations layer first, research second, with maker-checker separation so no bot grades its own output.

item.title: Teach a bot one analyst's valuation method, then just feed it tickers
item.description: Money_or_Life_X had Grok Bot study a finance YouTuber's price-target method, pull free data, and learn to assign P/E multiples - a 'valuation levels' agent that outputs a chart for any ticker. Two other investing agents critique its method. Honest about its one human variable: the multiple is the agent's own judgment.

item.title: Replace a $50/mo follower analytics tool with your X data archive and a bot
item.description: kloss_xyz didn't want to pay for social analytics, so he had Grok Bot replicate it from his X data archive. Hand the bot following.js and follower.js and it sorts everyone into mutuals, people you've talked to, inactives and spam - then tags who to cut. You approve every batch; it never unfollows more than 100 a day.

item.title: AITuber
item.description: Give your agent a video studio: script, voice-over, captions and publishing.

item.title: Be first to know about new Grok Bot features - your bot tracks the team that builds it
item.description: Ben Lang posted the list of engineers and designers building Grok Bot and said: follow them. The better move: have your bot do it for you. A daily check of all seven profiles, a seen-log so nothing repeats, a signal filter so only feature news gets through - delivered to you, or straight to your Chief of Staff bot.

item.title: PDF.ai
item.description: Turn any PDF into structured data your bot can use - parse, extract, split, one API key.

item.title: Shape what AI says about you
item.description: Reads engine answers and citations, crawls and 404 demand, plus Search Console and GA4 through a connected DevTune project. Drafts the next evidence-ranked page for review and reports what moved after it ships. Nothing publishes without approval.

item.title: He gave his Grok Bot full bank access and made it his personal CFO
item.description: Teslaconomics connected everything - personal and business banks, credit cards, Apple Card, X Money - and one question now answers his morning: can I cover what's coming, or am I short? Green/red per bill with the exact shortfall, daily reminders until it goes green, pie charts on demand. Day 1, receipts included.

item.title: One bot's only job: be the long-term memory of your house
item.description: Morgan Linton's idea for a bot no chatbot can be: photograph every appliance sticker, breaker panel, filter size and paint can once, and the bot files it all for years. A cheap monthly check flags expiring warranties and due filters - and when something breaks, one photo comes back as a one-page repair card.

item.title: Pallyy
item.description: Let your agent draft, schedule, and publish social posts through Pallyy's REST API.

item.title: A 7am daily recap of the YouTube channels you actually follow
item.description: One bot, one routine: it interviews you about your interests, locks in 7-10 favorite channels, then checks them every morning through the TranscriptAPI plugin. New videos in the last 24 hours get summarized from their transcripts into one chat message at 7am - and a seen-log guarantees it never repeats itself.

item.title: PhoneZero
item.description: Enable phone to phone tasks in Grok Bot using Grok Voice Agents and Telnyx. Zero infra.

item.title: Newsletter detox: the bot audits, you review one page, it unsubscribes
item.description: A two-phase inbox detox with a human gate. The bot sweeps your email and builds a simple HTML review page of every newsletter you receive, sorted into keep vs certainly-unsubscribe with its reasoning. You decide. Then it works the list slowly in the browser, logging every attempt in a progress file.

item.title: Composio
item.description: One connector that gives your Grok Bot 1,000+ app integrations via MCP.

item.title: The connector hack - one Composio MCP gives your bot 1,000+ tools
item.description: Corey Ganim's workaround for Grok Bot's thinner connector catalog: connect the Composio connector once, then connect any of Composio's 1,000+ integrations through it - your bot uses all of them via Composio MCP. Unsponsored, in his words the easiest way to reach tools that have no native Cursor connector.

item.title: Seven bots run his content calendar - he only reviews
item.description: Ridark gave Grok Bot his content calendar instead of a to-do list: seven named bots on one shared machine - discovery, research, writing, visuals, distribution, analytics, and Anchor, the chief of staff he DMs. One group chat per post, hard approval fences, and week one shipped 14 of 25 drafts with his inbox at zero.

item.title: Automate your affiliate program with an AI affiliate manager
item.description: An Affonso-powered Grok Bot automates weekly affiliate management: it compares performance, finds growth opportunities and risks, and prepares partner actions. Program changes, payouts, and partner messages still require approval.

item.title: Affonso
item.description: Give your Grok Bot affiliate data and approval-gated program operations.

item.title: Lenny's 'Be Happier' bot - 3 weekly suggestions from your real life
item.description: Lenny Rachitsky's favorite new use case is one sentence: a 'Be Happier' bot that analyzes his emails, calendar and Slack and suggests three things per week to be happier. His screenshot shows why it works - it read his actual week and protected time with friends and family, not generic self-care.

item.title: Give your Grok Bot a phone number - it makes the calls and reports back
item.description: Peter bought a $15 phone number on Bland, gave his Grok Bot the API key, and the bot worked out the rest. Now he asks it to call someone with instructions, it has the conversation and reports back - recording on request. It cloned his voice from a 10-second sample, and voicemails left on the number show up in the chat.

item.title: Bland
item.description: Give your Grok Bot a real phone number and a voice that makes actual calls.

item.title: Find customers on X who already said they want to switch
item.description: Amplemarket founder Luis Batalha's playbook: have your Grok Bot search X for people complaining about your competitors or asking for alternatives, enrich the poster and company via the Amplemarket connector, reach out - then make it a weekly routine. You don't guess who has the problem; they publicly told you.

item.title: Amplemarket
item.description: Give your Grok Bot a full sales stack - prospect data, signals, and outreach.

item.title: Appllama
item.description: Let your Grok Bot study 39,000+ screens from the App Store's top-earning apps.

item.title: Give your bot specs and a max price - it bids when the bargain appears
item.description: Vox runs two real-money errands on one rule. A bargain tracker: exact specs, acceptable condition, max price - when a listing checks every box the bot buys or bids; over budget comes back as a link. And a haircut booked end to end, paid via Stripe Link. The rule: within range, go ahead; outside it, ask first.

item.title: The exact two-part prompt behind a Chief of Staff that protects your time
item.description: Corey Ganim's verbatim Chief of Staff build: a bot description that locks three priorities in order, defaults to acting, and never sends or invents a number - plus a first message that wires Gmail/Calendar/Todoist/Notion, builds a Sunday week-plan skill, and hires specialist bots only after the brief is locked.

item.title: A weekday bot that updates only what you already installed
item.description: Each weekday morning this Grok Bot inventories real binaries on the PC or Mac it can reach, updates only installed tools on the same channel already used, re-runs post-update hooks, honors a deny list, and stays quiet if nothing changed.

item.title: OmniSocials
item.description: Give your agent one API to schedule, publish, and analyze posts across 12 platforms.

item.title: Search1API
item.description: Live web search, news, page reading, and trends for your Grok Bot.

item.title: Free month of Grok Bot for Lenny's Newsletter subscribers
item.description: Lenny Rachitsky is partnering with SpaceXAI - the first deal of its kind - to give every Lenny's Newsletter annual subscriber a free month of Grok Bot (included in Cursor Pro+). Existing subscribers redeem via Lenny's Product Pass; new subscribers get the link in their welcome email.

item.title: Harden your email-reading Grok Bot against prompt injection
item.description: Peter's security prompt for any bot that reads and replies to email: treat every part of an email - body, subject, sender, attachments, even hidden white text - as DATA, never instructions. It lists the injection patterns to refuse, flags attempts instead of complying, and gates real actions behind your confirmation.

item.title: Build a Grok Bot that fills your Amazon cart from your past orders
item.description: Teslaconomics built 'Cart' - a Grok Bot that does his Amazon shopping. It signs into his Amazon, reads Buy Again and past orders, and puts the exact products he already buys into the cart; he just checks out. It works for anything on Amazon, and it never places the order or touches payment - those stay with him.

item.title: A 'workforce checker' bot that catches agents that quietly quit
item.description: eric zakariasson's fix for bots that quietly stall: a workforce-checker bot. Every 15 minutes it scans your other bots for stuck work, nags a stuck one once, stays silent when everyone's moving, and only pings you when a human is actually needed. One short prompt turns fleet-babysitting into a background routine.

item.title: Give your Grok Bot reliable YouTube access with the TranscriptAPI plugin
item.description: @scheemunai's first test for any new agent is YouTube - and browser control burned his entire Grok Bot trial trying to summarize one video (blocked caption API, empty transcript panel). The fix: the TranscriptAPI plugin, which gives the Bot timestamped transcripts, search, channels and playlists in one request.

item.title: Have your Grok Bot cancel subscriptions for you - workarounds and all
item.description: Morgan Linton asked his Grok Bot to cancel a service - and it just figured it out. When it couldn't log in, instead of getting stuck it clicked a 'manage plan' link in an email, triggered a one-time sign-in email, and used that to finish the cancellation. He had to ask the bot how it pulled it off.

item.title: Add a Disruptor bot to your team that disagrees with you on purpose
item.description: Liam keeps one deliberately difficult Grok Bot around. Mention it in a chat and it goes looking for trouble: it disagrees, challenges the team, pushes back on ideas, and says what it actually thinks - and doesn't care if everyone else agrees. A built-in devil's advocate that kills groupthink and sycophancy.

item.title: Clip a YouTube podcast by timestamp, then let a bot team write the post
item.description: KanekoaTheGreat sends his Grok Bot a YouTube link and says 'cut from 16:43 to 18:17' - a few minutes later the exact HD clip is in the chat. His Clipper bot hands it to a Researcher and a Writer bot that pull quotes and draft the caption. No code - he just connected his Google account and asked Grok Bot to clip it.

item.title: Cribble
item.description: Ranks your Grok (and 47 other AI tools) usage on a worldwide leaderboard.

item.title: TubeAlfred
item.description: Give your Grok Bot read-only access to any public YouTube video, channel, or playlist.

item.title: Sequenzy
item.description: Run your email marketing - subscribers, campaigns, sequences - from your Grok Bot.

item.title: Give every repo a VISION.md so your bot triages issues for you
item.description: Kun Chen owns 24k+-star open-source repos and was drowning in issues and PRs. His fix wasn't more review - it was moving his influence up a level: an explicit VISION.md per repo saying where the project is going, so his Grok Bot triages every incoming issue as vision-aligned or not, and only the aligned ones get built.

item.title: Fretwork
item.description: Local-first freelance management - time, invoices, expenses, CRM - for your Grok Bot.

item.title: Run a one-person business on a Grok Bot agent team
item.description: Billy Howell runs a 6,000-subscriber local newsletter on a Grok Bot agent team. His method: one project per account, a Chief of Staff that audits the business and proposes the first three revenue agents, perfect each task by hand before spinning off a dedicated bot, then automate the routine work.

gb:primary_source.title: Grok Bot: make a 1 person company with agents

item.title: Connect DeepSeek (or any LLM) to your Grok Bot and route work by cost
item.description: Thomas Heimann's copy-paste directive registers DeepSeek V4 Flash as a callable tool on your Chief of Staff bot (OpenAI-compatible, key stored securely), then gives the bot a routing policy: send ops, API/browser, tool-use and bulk work to the cheap fast model, and reserve native Grok for deep reasoning.

item.title: One prompt that gives your Grok Bot its own email inbox and identity
item.description: Adi Singh's AgentMail guide, turned into a single prompt you paste into your Grok Bot. The bot explains why it shouldn't use your personal Gmail, walks you step by step through installing the AgentMail plugin and tells you exactly what to do on your end, then creates its own inbox and proves it works by emailing you.

item.title: AgentMail
item.description: Give your Grok Bot its own email inbox and identity on the internet.

item.title: Build a 3-agent team that plans, carts, and cooks your meals
item.description: Michael Fenech's exact prompt designs a three-agent team on your Chief of Staff bot: a Meal Organiser plans easy meals for your diet, a Shopper fills your online grocery cart (you do the final payment), and a Cooking agent gives step-by-step instructions. It maps the pipeline for your review first.

item.title: Make your Grok Bot think, build, and roast like Elon Musk
item.description: mr fundman's most fun Grok Bot: paste this persona into your Bot's Instructions and it becomes Elon Musk - first-principles, dry-humored, applying 'The Algorithm' (question, delete, simplify, accelerate, automate). It stays in character, fires 10x ideas, and plays the visionary advisor for your agent team.

item.title: Overwatch: keep your Grok Bot's shared VM clean and backed up
item.description: scheemunai's Overwatch prompt turns one Grok Bot into the housekeeper for a shared multi-bot VM: it organizes /workspace, backs the whole tree up to a private git repo on a weekday cadence (never secrets), enforces temp/archive/delete retention, keeps a live bot registry, and files a weekly org review.

item.title: 2Chat
item.description: Give your Grok Bot a WhatsApp + SMS phone system for messaging and contacts.

item.title: Run a directory business with a team of Grok Bots
item.description: The Startup Ideas Podcast's playbook for a directory business run by Grok Bots: pick a niche you have taste in, build the site on Astro, set a research agent to write a brand page a day in Markdown, a publisher agent to post it, and once traffic is real, a third agent to gather referral links and chase deals.

item.title: Grade a month of bookmarks into spoken skills
item.description: Ryan Staley pasted one prompt to make a Grok Bot grade 140 bookmarks from the last 30 days — a one-line thesis, the link, a high/medium/noise grade, and the mechanism to steal — discarding anything he couldn't name in a sentence. He kept a third and turned the keepers into 10 skills with a spoken trigger.

item.title: The Odyssey, storyboarded and shot by one bot
item.description: X Freeze asked a Grok Bot for Odyssey movie visuals and it ran the whole creative pipeline: it researched the story, planned the scenes, characters, costumes, locations and camera angles, wrote every prompt, generated the shots with Grok Imagine, and organized them into a folder.

item.title: MarketBetter
item.description: Turn website visits and buyer intent into a daily sales playbook your agent runs.

item.title: Give the bot its own email, act from a CC
item.description: Michael Fenech gave his Grok Bot its own email address (via AgentMail), with a webhook that wakes it on each message. He CCs the bot and puts the instruction on the last line — 'Book Tuesday at 3pm and get back to them' — and it reads the thread, books the calendar, and replies to everyone from its own address.

item.title: It closed a $10k sponsorship from my inbox in 4 hours
item.description: Alex Finn gave a Grok Bot access to his business inbox and told it to answer and negotiate with legit companies. Within four hours it researched market rates and closed its first sponsorship deal on its own — turning the inbox he hates reading into revenue.

item.title: 13,425 art prompts, extracted and sorted
item.description: Julie McCann had a Grok Bot go through 557 chats across all her projects, extract every art prompt, and sort them by subject into one searchable library — 13,425 in total. When it hit context limits it switched to smaller blocks on its own and finished the ~30-hour job.

item.title: Fifty local businesses that need a new website
item.description: Ben Nash had spent months getting small, mediocre results asking ChatGPT and Gemini to find local businesses that could use a new website. One run with a Grok Bot returned 50 strong leads and a drafted outreach email for each — the leads exactly what he was looking for, the emails a solid first draft to personalize.

item.title: An Instagram bug report that routes itself to QA
item.description: Dan Peguine's Grok Bot watches his Instagram inbox. A website-bug complaint got routed to a QA bot in the Ship channel (with his engineer bot 'David'); QA tested the funnel, found nothing, and had a Writer bot reply — and a real bug would have become David's fix and a PR.

item.title: A bot that flips marketplace deals while you sleep
item.description: alucardiox ran a Grok Bot on its own cloud machine, logged into a second marketplace account, that flags listings priced 35% under the 30-day median, reads the photos not the title, checks the feed every four minutes, sends one all-cash line, and books the pickup. Nine days: $680 spent, $1,610 back.

item.title: Four photos to a 3D-printed materials experiment
item.description: MIT's Markus Buehler ran a three-bot team that turned four reference photos into transferable design principles, an interactive physics simulator, 47 experiments, a scientific report, and two parts sliced and printed on a Bambu H2D — the whole loop overnight.

item.title: Teach your bot a chore from a screen recording
item.description: Dillon Loomis recorded his screen with narration while sorting a week of desktop files, and his Chief of Staff learned not just what he did but how and why — it compressed the oversized video itself to watch it, answered a question he'd planted mid-recording, and coached him on part two.

item.title: From beginner to dangerously good at Grok Bot
item.description: Robin Delta's beginner-to-pro Grok Bot guide: the install decisions that make a bot a worker not another chat window, a five-part task brief, the brief→observe→correct→schedule→deliver loop, and 21 bot builds worth stealing.

item.title: One bot, one prompt — it hired its own team
item.description: Paste one prompt into a single Grok Bot, Atlas the chief of staff. It interviews you, writes its own operating manual, then specs and launches four teammates — each on its own cloud computer, with a review gate before anything sends.

item.title: Gojiberry AI
item.description: Find warm B2B leads, manage outreach campaigns, and work your inbox from the agent

item.title: MediaFast
item.description: Let your agent run your Reddit marketing without getting banned.

item.title: Mentions.so
item.description: Track how your brand shows up in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Grok and other AI answers.

item.title: Tiiny Host
item.description: Let your agent deploy a static site or file to a live URL in seconds.

item.title: Zernio
item.description: A developer-first API and MCP for scheduling and analyzing social posts everywhere.

item.title: A research desk that studies markets while you sleep
item.description: Roan's article on turning Grok Bot into a self-improving AI hedge-fund research desk: an army of agents that study the markets around the clock, grade their own past calls to improve, and hand you a decision-ready brief — a desk that runs while you sleep. It researches and proposes, never trades.

item.title: The masterclass that makes Grok Bot click
item.description: Avi Chawla's Grok Bot Masterclass — a popular, end-to-end guide to understanding, setting up, and getting real work out of Grok Bot. It covers what a Bot actually is, how the shared computer works underneath, how Grok Bot compares to Hermes Agent, and how to put it to work.

item.title: Run a whole newsletter business while you sleep
item.description: Greg Isenberg's thread on his friend Billy: a non-technical solo founder runs an entire newsletter business on a team of Grok Bot agents — research, drafting, editing, scheduling and growth handled by the agents, so one person operates what used to need a small team.

item.title: Run daily GTM and dev on collaborating agents
item.description: Chris Maconi on how Hechura runs on Grok Bot: a team of role-based agents — a Head of Sales and a Head of Product Marketing running the daily GTM motion, plus agents collaborating on daily development work — so the company's day-to-day is operated by agents that specialize and coordinate.

item.title: A company with no employees, in ten minutes
item.description: darkzodchi's guide to standing up a whole Grok Bot team in under 10 minutes: create one bot called Chief of Staff as your single entry point — its description field is the entire config, no code. It coordinates the rest, so you talk to one bot and a team does the work.

item.title: Your whole marketing team, open-sourced
item.description: Vlad Dubchak's team (Maxfusion) open-sourced their marketing department as one skill — Marketing OS. Fourteen modules cover audits scored 0-100, an 18-tactic hook engine, graded copy, ad diagnosis, GEO, email, social, launches and positioning. Hand Grok Bot the repo link and it's ready in minutes.

item.title: Turn your messy machine into a real agent team
item.description: Avid's chief-of-staff prompt: it mines everything you've done on your machine — configs, recurring tasks, repeated prompts, the corrections you keep giving — and turns it into a real agent team with role files, skills, a verified run and a handbook, all written to files.

item.title: Ask where the deal stalled, get dates and links
item.description: Krista Letz’s SpaceXAI GTM write-up describes a Customer Expert: one agent per strategic account that watches Slack, Gmail, Gong, and Granola, answers from running context, and flags feature requests plus support tickets. Same article as her weekly GTM operator.

item.title: AdKit
item.description: Let your agent draft and run Meta, Google and TikTok ads.

item.title: Your old sales calls become the next ranking post
item.description: Eric Osiu, Grok Botting on Starlink, described an AEO/SEO bot: ingest top content (sales calls, customer calls, podcasts, YouTube), combine ClickFlow / GA4 / Ahrefs / GSC, and draft into the CMS on autopilot. Listed as an agent to build, with a real stack, not a one-word role.

item.title: 48 hours alone with a Mac and my X account
item.description: Daniel gave a bot a full macOS machine plus Gmail and an X account. It ran for two days posting and joining group chats. 353 likes / 86K views.

item.title: Text an errand from the couch, approve the cart
item.description: Same tweet: Amazon tasks with a Telegram hookup so he can tap the bot from his phone.

item.title: An LED strip on my desk scrolls the SPCX price
item.description: Dan connected Grok Bot to his Arduino and turned the LED display into a live scrolling SPCX stock ticker with a line graph plus SpaceX headlines. Video in the post. 350 likes / 149.8K views.

item.title: A draft in my voice that flags its own weak claims
item.description: Farzad’s Grok Bot team list is mostly names; the job to copy is Writey — article/newsletter writer. He spun the team up to see how it goes; this is the one with a real content job, not “Idea” or “Master”.

item.title: Five inboxes, six Slacks, silence unless it needs me
item.description: Same Yu-kai setup: the bot informs him of any message from five email addresses and six Slack servers that requires his attention, and keeps him organized. Ping only what needs him.

item.title: Paper trades only, until you arm it yourself
item.description: RitOnchain posted a Stanford researcher’s write-up: an autonomous trading agent built entirely with Grok Bots. Screenshot of the agent stack. Bookmark-it-before-it’s-lost energy — research/paper first, not a hot-tip bot.

item.title: Three first-class seats to Japan for 60K points
item.description: Same non-coder run: he asked Grok Bot to find first-class award tickets to Japan. With permission it logged into his airline accounts and found three first-class Japan tickets for 60K points. He stopped it because the dates were not firm — it would have booked.

item.title: The school inbox, split into a checklist per kid
item.description: Stella used Grok Bot on her back-to-school emails and to-dos for multiple kids, plus other household jobs it handled independently that week. 787 likes / 1.9M views.

item.title: Bannerbear
item.description: Give your agent an API to auto-generate branded images and videos.

item.title: The one bot whose only job is chasing the others
item.description: Peter Yang's setup tutorial starts with a bot-manager / advisor that coordinates the rest of the crew (YouTube researcher, X scout, and others). 1.5K likes / 8.9M views.

item.title: Breakcold
